questions.text: An air capacitor charged to a potential difference of 800 V is connected in parallel with an uncharged capacitor of the same dimensions filled with a dielectric. If the potential difference after connecting the capacitors is 100 V, determine the dielectric constant of the dielectric.

A parallel-plate air capacitor is charged to a potential difference of 50 V and disconnected from the source. A metal sheet 1 mm thick is then inserted between the capacitor plates, parallel to them. If the distance between the plates is 5 mm, determine the potential difference between the capacitor plates (V).

Two identical capacitors are connected in parallel and charged to a potential difference of 6 V. After the capacitors are disconnected from the source, the distance between the plates of one of them is halved. Determine the potential difference between the capacitor plates (V).

A voltmeter connected in parallel with a 12 $\mu F$ capacitor attached to a DC source reads 3 V. What voltage (V) will the voltmeter read if a second capacitor of 8 $\mu F$ is connected in parallel with this capacitor?
What is the ordered motion of charged particles called?
What is the main sign of an electric current?
answers: The presence of a magnetic field around it.
The presence of a gravitational field around it.
The presence of a potential field around it.
The presence of a vortex field around it.

questions.text: Indicate the correct statement.
answers: Current is a positive scalar quantity.
The sign of the current is determined by the sign of the charge carriers.
Current is a scalar but signed (algebraic) quantity.

questions.text: What is called current density?
answers: the charge passing through the surface of a conductor per unit time...
the charge displaced by 1 m along a conductor per unit time...
the charge passing through the cross-section of a conductor per unit time...
a vector quantity equal to the charge passing per unit time through a unit area of the conductor's cross-section.

questions.text: A current of 10 A flows through a conductor. Find the total mass of electrons passing through the cross-section of this conductor in 1 hour (mg). $e = 1.6 \cdot 10^{-19} \, C, m_e = 9.1 \cdot 10^{-31} \, kg$.
How many electrons pass through the cross-section of a conductor in 1 ns when the current is 32 $\mu A$?
Determine the number of electrons passing through the cross-section of a conductor in 1 ms when the current is 16 mA. $e = 1.6 \cdot 10^{-19} \, C$.
A current of 1 A flowed through a conductor for 24 hours. Find the mass of electrons (mg) that passed through the conductor's cross-section during this time. $e/m_e = 1.76 \cdot 10^{11} \, C/kg$.
If the current in a conductor increased linearly from 0 to 5 A in 10 s, how much charge (C) flowed through the conductor's cross-section during this time?
In an electrolytic bath containing zinc sulfate, the current varies linearly as $I = (2 + 0.02t) \, A$. Determine the electric charge that passed through the electrolyte in 5 min (C).
The current in a circuit increases according to the law $I = 10^{-6}t$. How many electrons passed through the circuit in 1.5 minutes?
The current in a section of a circuit increased uniformly from 0 to 1.5 A in 6 s. Indicate the graph of current versus time (based on the graphs in Source [3]).
A capacitor of 200 $\mu F$ is charged to a voltage of 5000 V in 5 s. Find the average charging current (A).
If a charge of 20 C passed through a conductor's cross-section of 5 $mm^2$ in 8 s, what is the current density ($A/m^2$)?

A current of 3 A flows through a copper wire with a cross-sectional area of 20 $mm^2$. Find the speed of the conduction electrons in it ($m/s$). The number of free electrons per unit volume is $9 \cdot 10^{28} \, m^{-3}$.

A current of 3 A flows through a metal conductor with a cross-sectional area of 0.5 $mm^2$. If the concentration of free electrons in the metal is $4 \cdot 10^{28} \, m^{-3}$, find the average drift speed of the electrons ($mkm/s$).
